attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. 'As I said a few weeks ago' repeats his own earlier view, so it is still his claim.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: there is no firm understanding of AI compute, and Microsoft is actively misleading the public about capacity coming online. The wording is firm and present-tense, so it is an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'firm understanding' as a reliable public account, and requiring an identifiable misleading Microsoft statement, is an ordinary reading. The result does depend on how 'firm' and 'misleading' are read.

evidence.note: Microsoft's July 29 earnings call says it added a gigawatt of overall capacity. This shows what Microsoft said, but nothing checks it against operational records, so it neither proves nor disproves misleading.

Epoch's September 9 explorer gives modelled compute estimates with uncertainty. It shows public estimates exist but have limits. It does not settle 'firm understanding' and says nothing about Microsoft misrepresenting capacity.

reviews.rationale: No complete operational inventory and no commissioning record that tests Microsoft's capacity statements. The Bloomberg and Reuters sources were unreadable. The packet shows uncertainty and one company statement, but cannot establish either a material misrepresentation or that the statement was accurate.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent: startups can no longer keep raising money. 'Disappear' is firm, unhedged language, so this is a scoreable conditional forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: Turning 'unlimited money' into a real loss of fundraising access, and 'large chunks' into material realized revenue loss, is a fair reading. No threshold or time lag was stated, so the reading shapes any result.

evidence.note: CB Insights Q3 2026: AI funding fell 33% but investors are still backing new unicorns. That points to continued access to money, so the antecedent has not been shown to occur.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, startups losing fundraising access, is not established, and no records show revenue lost after such an event. Under policy a conditional is not scored while its antecedent is unknown. No deadline was given, so the forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence summarising his argument.

semantics.note: Keeps 'massive', 'without restraint' and 'every release'. It is a causal claim about how releases drive revenue through startup spending.

contract.note: The plain reading (each release causes substantial extra realized revenue through subsidized startup use) is ordinary. With this evidence the result would be unresolved under any reasonable reading.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 (filed Oct 26) links revenue growth to new model releases. But it does not trace that growth to startup subsidies or show it for every release, and it covers Anthropic only.
Ramp data show August spending by top-1% firms fell, with seasonality and price cuts as possible reasons. It cannot isolate any release or either provider's revenue.

reviews.rationale: The S-1 partly backs a link between releases and revenue for Anthropic. Nothing establishes the startup-funded mechanism, the 'every release' scope, or anything for OpenAI. There is no release-by-release revenue attribution, so the causal claim is neither supported nor contradicted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Captures the core claims: no product-market fit, cannot support itself, wholly dependent on venture capital. It leaves out the claimed fundraising pattern (at least $160M every three to six months), but the contract restores it.

contract.note: Reading product-market fit as demand at sustainable prices matches the speaker's own gloss. 'Cannot support itself' is read as operations, not gross margin. Using the July–September 2026 quarter is a reasonable choice, but it is an evaluator choice.

evidence.note: Harvey announced a $550M raise on September 9, 2026. That confirms continued venture funding but not that the company needs it to survive.

Bloomberg Línea, citing unnamed sources, says Harvey's gross margins turned positive after its August model launch; Harvey would not comment. This weakens the claim only slightly, because positive gross margin does not show operating self-sufficiency.

reviews.rationale: No operating accounts, cash-flow figures, retention or pricing data, and no complete record of fundraising since February 2025. The packet shows heavy fundraising and a reported gross-margin recovery. Neither establishes or refutes that Harvey cannot sustain itself without venture money or lacks product-market fit.
